at-0001.title: Round money only with round_money
at-0001.content: Always round monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.

Check the key first, before validating state: if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result (for functions that return a record, the same record) without applying the operation again. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.

at-0002.title: Normalize money via to_money and round_money
at-0002.content: In ledgerly/invoice.py, convert any monetary input with to_money() and store it rounded with round_money(); compare against ZERO from ledgerly.money rather than raw numbers.

at-0003.content: Reject invalid billing input by raising BillingError(code, detail) from ledgerly.errors with codes like "invalid_state", "invalid_quantity" and "negative_amount", matching the existing issue_invoice pattern.

at-0004.title: Exclude bool when validating integer fields
at-0004.content: When validating integer fields such as quantity, reject bool explicitly (isinstance(x, bool)) before the int check, since True/False are ints in Python.

at-0005.title: Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc
at-0005.content: In ledgerly, normalize every incoming datetime with `ensure_utc` from `ledgerly.clock` before comparing or doing arithmetic (see `current_period` in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py`). Apply it to both the argument and `sub.started_at`.

at-0006.title: Compute periods with timedelta floor division
at-0006.content: Compute subscription period boundaries the same way as `current_period` in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py`: `length = timedelta(days=sub.period_days)` and `n = (at - start) // length`, then `start + n * length`.
